dialogue.origin: こんにちは。本日はよろしくお願い致します。
dialogue.content: Hello. I look forward to working with you today.

dialogue.origin: こんにちは。こちらこそ、よろしくお願い致します。
dialogue.content: Hello. Likewise, I look forward to it.

dialogue.origin: 時間になりましたら始めさせていただたいと思います。
dialogue.content: I'd like to get started now that it's time.

dialogue.origin: はい、お願い致します。
dialogue.content: Yes, please.

dialogue.origin: こんにちは。相談員です。本日は相談に起こしいただきありがとうございます。　　　最初に年齢と性別を教えていただけますか？
dialogue.content: Hello. I'm the counselor. Thank you for coming in for a consultation today. First, could you please tell me your age and gender?

dialogue.origin: 17歳　女子高生です
dialogue.content: I'm a 17-year-old high school girl.

dialogue.origin: ありがとうございます。本日はどのようなご相談ですか？
dialogue.content: Thank you. What would you like to talk about today?

dialogue.origin: 母親が大嫌いです
dialogue.content: I really hate my mother.

dialogue.origin: そうなんですね。お話を詳しくお話を聞かせてください
dialogue.content: I see. Could you tell me more about that?

dialogue.origin: 三人兄弟の真ん中で、姉と弟がいます
dialogue.content: I'm the middle child of three siblings, and I have an older sister and a younger brother.

dialogue.origin: ええ
dialogue.content: Mm-hmm.

dialogue.origin: 姉と弟は成績優秀で、私はおバカです
dialogue.content: My sister and brother get excellent grades, and I’m the dumb one.

dialogue.origin: いつも比較をしてきます
dialogue.content: She always compares me to them.

dialogue.origin: そうなんですね。
dialogue.content: I see.

dialogue.origin: それは辛いですね
dialogue.content: That must be difficult.

dialogue.origin: 姉も弟も生徒会やったり、成績もトップクラス
dialogue.content: My sister and brother are on the student council and get top grades.

dialogue.origin: 私は下の方の成績です
dialogue.content: My grades are near the bottom.

dialogue.origin: 家にいたくないです
dialogue.content: I don’t want to be at home.

dialogue.origin: そうお感じなのですね。。
dialogue.content: So that's how you feel.

dialogue.origin: それはモヤモヤしてしまいますね
dialogue.content: That must be very frustrating.

dialogue.origin: 家でも何回も考えましたが、行くとこないので…
dialogue.content: I’ve thought about it many times at home, but I have nowhere to go…

dialogue.origin: 家出です
dialogue.content: Running away from home.

dialogue.origin: 家出をしたいくらい居心地が悪いとお感じなのですね
dialogue.content: So you feel so uncomfortable at home that you want to run away.

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: それは苦しいですね
dialogue.content: That must be painful.

dialogue.origin: あの人の顔見てるとイライラしてくる
dialogue.content: Just looking at her face irritates me.

dialogue.origin: ええ、そう感じるのですね。
dialogue.content: I see, so that's how you feel.

dialogue.origin: あの人は自分が全て正しいと思っていて、私の話なんか聞いてくれない
dialogue.content: She thinks she's always right and never listens to what I have to say.

dialogue.origin: どうせおバカの言う事だから
dialogue.content: Because it's just the stupid one talking.

dialogue.origin: どのようなやり取りがあったかお話できる範囲で聞かせてもらえますか？
dialogue.content: Could you tell me about any interactions you've had, to the extent that you're comfortable sharing?

dialogue.origin: 小さい頃、姉が学校で私に嫌がらせをして来て、母に言ったら「お姉ちゃんがそんな事するはずない」と信じてもらえなかった
dialogue.content: When I was little, my sister was bullying me at school, and when I told my mom, she didn't believe me, saying, "Your older sister would never do something like that."

dialogue.origin: 姉も大嫌い
dialogue.content: I really hate my sister, too.

dialogue.origin: そんなことがあったのですね。。
dialogue.content: So that's what happened...

dialogue.origin: 母親にいじめられてるのを見て、笑ってる
dialogue.content: She watches my mother bully me and laughs.

dialogue.origin: 姉は母親から、絶対的信用されてるので、私は信じてもらえない
dialogue.content: My sister has my mother's absolute trust, so I'm never believed.

dialogue.origin: そう感じているんだね。。苦しいね
dialogue.content: That's how you feel... That must be painful.

dialogue.origin: どこに出しても恥ずかしくない娘だと言ってる
dialogue.content: She says my sister is a daughter she wouldn't be ashamed of anywhere.

dialogue.origin: 私はどこに出しても恥ずかしいって
dialogue.content: And that I'm an embarrassment wherever I go.

dialogue.origin: 嘘つきな奴なのに
dialogue.content: Even though she’s a liar.

dialogue.origin: ええ
dialogue.content: Mm-hmm.

dialogue.origin: 母親は私なんか居なくても何とも思わないんだと思う
dialogue.content: I think my mother wouldn’t care at all if I weren’t around.

dialogue.origin: 私のこと、馬鹿な子、ブスな子と言います
dialogue.content: She calls me a stupid kid, an ugly kid.

dialogue.origin: ええ。聞いています
dialogue.content: Mm-hmm. I'm listening.

dialogue.origin: もう嫌だ
dialogue.content: I can't take it anymore.

dialogue.origin: この先生きていく意味ある？
dialogue.content: Is there any point in going on living?

dialogue.origin: そんなひどい事を言われたら落ち込むのも無理ないね
dialogue.content: It's no wonder you feel down after being told such awful things.

dialogue.origin: とても悲しいですね…
dialogue.content: That's very sad...

dialogue.origin: 学校の行事で、家族からの手紙をもらうことがあって、友達は感動的な事書いてあったけど
dialogue.content: At a school event, we received letters from our families, and my friends' letters had touching things written in them,

dialogue.origin: 母親は、私の悪いところばっかり書いてあった
dialogue.content: but my mother's letter was just full of my faults.

dialogue.origin: 直しなさいと
dialogue.content: Telling me to fix them.

dialogue.origin: うんうん
dialogue.content: Mm-hmm.

dialogue.origin: 友達、みんな見せ合ってたけど、
dialogue.content: All my friends were showing theirs to each other, but…

dialogue.origin: 私は恥ずかしくて、見せれなかった
dialogue.content: I was too embarrassed to show mine.

dialogue.origin: いつも喧嘩になる
dialogue.content: We always end up fighting.

dialogue.origin: そうでしたか…
dialogue.content: I see…

dialogue.origin: 母親は過干渉で、自分の思い通りにならないと気が済まない
dialogue.content: My mother is overbearing and isn't satisfied unless she gets her way.

dialogue.origin: だから、問題児の私が憎らしい
dialogue.content: That's why she hates me, the problem child.

dialogue.origin: ちなみにあなたの事をなんとお呼びしたらいいですか？
dialogue.content: By the way, what should I call you?

dialogue.origin: 友希
dialogue.content: Yuki.

dialogue.origin: 友希さんですね、ありがとうございます
dialogue.content: Yuki, thank you.

dialogue.origin: もう何もかもどうでもいい
dialogue.content: I don’t care about anything anymore.

dialogue.origin: うんうん
dialogue.content: Mm-hmm.

dialogue.origin: これまでのお話をまとめてみてもいいですか？
dialogue.content: May I summarize what I’ve heard so far?

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: 友希さんはお母さんの事が大嫌いで悩んでおられます。自分以外の兄弟二人は成績もよくお母さんに好かれていて自分は嫌われている
dialogue.content: Yuki, you're struggling because you really hate your mother. Your two siblings get good grades and are liked by your mother, while you feel that you are disliked.

dialogue.origin: そうです
dialogue.content: That’s right.

dialogue.origin: 家での居心地が悪く家でも考えるほどです
dialogue.content: You feel so uncomfortable at home that you've even considered running away.

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: 友希さんはお母さんにとてもひどい事を言われてとても悩んでおられて、生きていく意味も分からないし、
dialogue.content: You are deeply troubled by the terrible things your mother says to you, to the point where you don't see the meaning in life,

dialogue.origin: どうしたらいいかわからないとお感じです。
dialogue.content: and you feel like you don't know what to do.

dialogue.origin: そうです
dialogue.content: That’s right.

dialogue.origin: お母さんに優しくしてもらえないととても苦しく、悲しいですね。
dialogue.content: Not being treated kindly by your mother is very painful and sad.

dialogue.origin: それに腹も立ちますね
dialogue.content: And it must make you angry, too.

dialogue.origin: 私には優しくなんて何があってもしません
dialogue.content: She would never be kind to me, no matter what.

dialogue.origin: 憎しみしかないです
dialogue.content: All I feel is hatred.

dialogue.origin: そうお感じなのですね。
dialogue.content: That’s how you feel.

dialogue.origin: 態度で分かります
dialogue.content: I can tell from her attitude.

dialogue.origin: うんうん
dialogue.content: Mm-hmm.

dialogue.origin: 私なんか生まれて来なければ良かった
dialogue.content: I wish I had never been born.

dialogue.origin: そしたら母親にとって、家族は自慢の子供たちだけで
dialogue.content: Then, for my mother, the family would be only the children she could be proud of,

dialogue.origin: 邪魔者はいなくなる
dialogue.content: and the nuisance would be gone.

dialogue.origin: そう感じているのですね。でも無駄な命なんてありません
dialogue.content: That's how you feel. But no life is worthless.

dialogue.origin: 友希さんのお話を伺っていて
dialogue.content: Listening to what you’ve shared, Yuki,

dialogue.origin: お母さんに自分の事をわかって欲しい、見てほしいと感じているように思うのですがいかがでしょうか？
dialogue.content: I get the sense that you want your mother to understand you and see you for who you are. How does that sound?

dialogue.origin: もう諦めていますどうせ無理だから
dialogue.content: I've already given up because it's impossible anyway.

dialogue.origin: ひどい事をいわれ続けているとそう思ってしまいますよね
dialogue.content: When you're constantly told such awful things, it's natural to start thinking that way.

dialogue.origin: 苦しいし、無理もないと思います。
dialogue.content: It's painful, and I think it's completely understandable.

dialogue.origin: 母親、自分の意見を曲げないところは、見事です
dialogue.content: My mother’s refusal to back down from her opinions is impressive, in a way.

dialogue.origin: あんな人間、見たことない
dialogue.content: I’ve never seen anyone like her.

dialogue.origin: うんうん
dialogue.content: Mm-hmm.

dialogue.origin: いろんな考えの人がいる事を知らない
dialogue.content: She doesn't know that people have different ways of thinking.

dialogue.origin: 私が自分の意見を言うと、だから馬鹿なんだと言う
dialogue.content: When I express my own opinion, she says, "That’s why you’re stupid."

dialogue.origin: 太刀打ちできない
dialogue.content: There's no arguing with her.

dialogue.origin: そうなんですね。でも色々考えの人がいることをわかって欲しいですね
dialogue.content: I see. But it would be good if she understood that people have different ways of thinking.

dialogue.origin: あの人を何とかしようと考えるだけ、無駄なパワーを使う
dialogue.content: Just thinking about trying to change her is a waste of energy.

dialogue.origin: アスファルトを素手で掘ろうとしてるくらい
dialogue.content: It’s like trying to dig through asphalt with your bare hands.

dialogue.origin: 諦めた方がいい
dialogue.content: It's better to give up.

dialogue.origin: ええ。人を変えるのはとても難しいことだとおもいます
dialogue.content: Yes. I think changing another person is very difficult.

dialogue.origin: 少し友希さんの事を教えてください
dialogue.content: Could you tell me a bit about yourself, Yuki?

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Okay.

dialogue.origin: 高校では部活はしていますねか？
dialogue.content: Are you in any clubs at high school?

dialogue.origin: はい、テニス部です
dialogue.content: Yes, I’m in the tennis club.

dialogue.origin: 部活は楽しいですか？
dialogue.content: Do you enjoy the club?

dialogue.origin: はい、友達がいるので、学校も楽しいです。家にはいたくないから
dialogue.content: Yes. I have friends there, so school is fun. And I don’t want to be at home.

dialogue.origin: 不登校の反対
dialogue.content: The opposite of skipping school.

dialogue.origin: そうなんですね
dialogue.content: I see.

dialogue.origin: だから、絶対に不登校にはならない
dialogue.content: So, I'll absolutely never skip school.

dialogue.origin: 学校が楽しいのはとてもいいことですね
dialogue.content: It's great that you enjoy school.

dialogue.origin: 自分に楽しいと思える居場所があるのですから
dialogue.content: Because you have a place where you can feel happy.

dialogue.origin: これで学校も辛かったら、最悪
dialogue.content: If school were tough too, that would be the worst.

dialogue.origin: うちではお母さんとは仲が良くないみたいだけど
dialogue.content: It sounds like you don't get along with your mother at home,

dialogue.origin: お父さんや他の家族とはどうですか？
dialogue.content: how are things with your father and other family members?

dialogue.origin: お父さんは大好き。というか、お父さんもお母さんにいじめられてるので、可哀想に思う。
dialogue.content: I love my dad. Or rather, I feel sorry for him, because my mother bullies him too.

dialogue.origin: そうなんですね
dialogue.content: I see.

dialogue.origin: 弟は、男だから　比べられても、そんなに気にならないかな…
dialogue.content: As for my brother, he's a boy, so maybe he doesn't mind being compared as much...

dialogue.origin: ええ
dialogue.content: Mm-hmm.

dialogue.origin: 姉とは、掃除の仕方とか茶碗の洗い方とか、もちろん成績もだけど、気が利くとか比べられるから
dialogue.content: With my sister, I’m compared on things like how I clean, how I wash the dishes, grades of course, and whether I’m considerate.

dialogue.origin: でも姉のがブスだと思うけど
dialogue.content: But I think my sister is uglier.

dialogue.origin: お父さんは友希さんとは話しますか？
dialogue.content: Do you and your father talk?

dialogue.origin: 話します
dialogue.content: We do talk.

dialogue.origin: そうなんですね。理解してくれていると感じますか？
dialogue.content: I see. Do you feel that he understands you?

dialogue.origin: 理解はどうかな
dialogue.content: I’m not sure about understanding.

dialogue.origin: お父さん、ちょっと障害があるっぽいから
dialogue.content: My dad seems to have some sort of disability.

dialogue.origin: そうなんですね。
dialogue.content: I see.

dialogue.origin: だからお母さんに馬鹿にされてる
dialogue.content: That's why my mother looks down on him.

dialogue.origin: ええ、それを見ているのは辛いですね
dialogue.content: Mm-hmm, it must be painful to watch that.

dialogue.origin: 可哀想です
dialogue.content: I feel sorry for him.

dialogue.origin: 大好きなお母さんが馬鹿にされているのを見ているのは可哀想と感じてしまいますね
dialogue.content: Watching your beloved mother being belittled makes you feel sorry for her.

dialogue.origin: お父さんですね
dialogue.content: You mean my father.

dialogue.origin: 失礼致しました大きな間違いでした
dialogue.content: My apologies, that was a big mistake.

dialogue.origin: 大丈夫です
dialogue.content: It’s okay.

dialogue.origin: 友希さんはとても正義感があり優しいかたなのが伝わってきます。
dialogue.content: I can tell you have a strong sense of justice and are a very kind person, Yuki.

dialogue.origin: とても強いお母さんの態度を変えることはすぐには難しいことかもしれませんが
dialogue.content: It might be difficult to immediately change your very strong-willed mother's attitude, but

dialogue.origin: 大好きなお父さんはいて、きっと友希さんの事を見てくれていると思います。学校は楽しくて、うち以外の以居心地のよい場所があって安心しました。
dialogue.content: you have a father you love, and I'm sure he is watching over you. I'm relieved to hear that you enjoy school and have a comfortable place to be outside of your home.

dialogue.origin: まあ、そうですね
dialogue.content: Well, I guess so.

dialogue.origin: 成績はお姉さんや弟さんに比べると悪いかもしれませんが、人の評価はそれだけではないと思います。
dialogue.content: Your grades may not be as good as your sister's or brother's, but I don't think a person's worth is measured by that alone.

dialogue.origin: 性格はブス姉よりマシかと思っています
dialogue.content: I think my personality is better than my ugly sister’s.

dialogue.origin: そうですね！　これまで通りテニスにも打ち込んで楽しい学校生活を送りながら、自分自身を高めていってください
dialogue.content: That's right! Please continue to devote yourself to tennis, enjoy your school life, and keep working on improving yourself.

dialogue.origin: 分かりました
dialogue.content: I understand.

dialogue.origin: それをお母さんが見てくれる日が来ることを願っています
dialogue.content: I hope the day will come when your mother notices that.

dialogue.origin: 今日はお時間がきてしまいましたが、他に何かお話したいことがなければこれで終了させていただきます
dialogue.content: Our time is up for today, but if there's nothing else you'd like to talk about, we can end here.

dialogue.origin: はい、ありがとうございました。
dialogue.content: Yes, thank you very much.

dialogue.origin: (ありがとうございました。勉強になりました。)
dialogue.content: (Thank you. This was a good learning experience.)

dialogue.origin: また何かありましたらご相談にいらしてください
dialogue.content: Please come back anytime if something else comes up.

dialogue.origin: （ありがとうございました。お疲れ様でした）
dialogue.content: (Thank you very much. Good work today.)

dialogue.origin: (お疲れ様でした)
dialogue.content: (Good work today.)

dialogue.origin: （時間が過ぎてしまいすみません。ロールプレイを終了させていただきますね。）
dialogue.content: (I’m sorry we ran over time. I’ll go ahead and end the role-play here.)

dialogue.origin: (こちらこそ、長くなってしまい、すみませんでした)
dialogue.content: (No, I'm sorry for making it run long.)
